title: Repacking a Leaky Shut-Off Valve with Teflon Packing
summary: This This Old House clip demonstrates repairing a leaky shut-off valve by rebuilding the bonnet packing with a new Teﬂon wrap. The presenters first shut off the main water supply, remove the bonnet nut with an open-end wrench, and note the absence of a gasket. They then apply Teﬂon packing around the spindle, reseat and tighten the bonnet, and finally reopen the main valve to verify that water flows normally without leaks. The sequence emphasizes careful wrapping of packing, thread alignment, and a cautious test to confirm a leak-free seal.

sections.title: Shutoff and bonnet access
sections.description: The operator shuts the main water supply and uses an open-end wrench to access the bonnet nut on the valve, preparing for disassembly. Notes that no gasket is present at the bonnet, implying replacement is needed.

sections.title: Install Teﬂon packing and reseat bonnet
sections.description: New Teﬂon packing is wrapped around the valve spindle and the bonnet is reinserted, with attention to catching the threads and seating the components for reassembly.

sections.title: Tighten, reopen, and test
sections.description: The bonnet nut is snugged by hand and then tightened with a wrench for a secure seal. The main shut-off valve is opened counterclockwise to restore pressure, and water flow is observed to confirm the repair is leak-free.

sections.title: Post-test wrap-up
sections.description: The video concludes with verification of restored flow and a light, non-technical wrap-up cue, including addressing incidental items (e.g., returning items to place) after the test.
